newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African farm minister recommits to free market.
newsitem.headline: S.African farm minister recommits to free market.

text.p: South African Land Affairs and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom on Friday reaffirmed his commitment to a free agricultural market where government intervention is kept to a minimum.
"Market forces should be the strongest determinant," Hanekom said addressing a foreign correspondents breakfast.
"The government will always play a role in marketing, for example, of exports, but we will not have a single channel marketing system and fixed pricing...Control boards are going to come to an end."

Parliament last week adopted the Marketing of Agricultural Products Bill which effectively signals the end of state-owned control board supremacy over agriculture, long the backbone of white commercial domination of the industry.
"Controls existed that were not rational and not in the interests of the economy. I don't only represent farmers, my key focus is the broader agricultural economy," Hanekom said.

The new bill, likely to be implemented next year, sets a 13-month timetable for the dismantling of remaining control boards which still dominate the production and marketing of commodities including fruit, cotton, maize, meat, mohair, lucerne, wheat, oilseeds and wool.

"Boards are preparing business plans to show how they plan to reorganise themselves in terms of the new bill. But the bill also allows for the minister to close any existing scheme if the board is not doing what is required," Hanekom said.

With the demise of control boards, farmers would have to seek alternative mechanisms to protect against crop failure, he said. "If a farmer plants too much maize, he will be in trouble. He must use other defence mechanisms such as (hedging) on the futures market."
The South African Futures Exchange last year launched an agricultural markets division which runs contracts in maize, beef and potatoes.
